scope: Initial 33-paper discussion-driven catalog plus a targeted 17-paper future-context, prompt-and-refine, emission-latency and distillation extension. Not an exhaustive systematic review or a novelty certification.

papers.title: Speculative Speech Recognition by Audio-Prefixed Low-Rank Adaptation of Language Models
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.evidence_location: PDF Page 1–4, Figure 1, Section 2.2, Eq. (8), Tables 1–3
papers.summary_en: Speculative Speech Recognition predicts an unheard continuation from observed audio and transcript.
papers.method_en: Connect a language model applying voice conditional soft prefix and LoRA to the Conformer-Transducer output. We also propose a learning label alignment that takes ASR errors into account.
papers.evidence_en: Evaluating speech conditional prediction in LibriSpeech and multi-domain experiments. The default SOWER setting is 1 seconds in the future, 8 candidates, and oracle evaluation to select the best candidate a posteriori.
papers.relevance_en: The closest prior work to preparing the next words and verifying them with new audio; it motivates a text-only versus audio-aware forecasting comparison.
papers.limitation_en: The SOWER improvement cannot be translated into a reduction in word commit latency in the actual system. This paper distinguishes the problem from general speculative decoding, which reduces the computation of a large model into a small model.

papers.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
papers.reading_depth: Bibliography, abstract, core sections and experimental setup checked; no exhaustive close reading or reproduction.
papers.code_note: Do not assume a public checkpoint exists.
papers.evidence_location: PDF 3–7 Page, Sections 3–5, Tables 1–2
papers.summary_en: Full-duplex speech-language-model research drafts during idle time before the next audio chunk and verifies after arrival.
papers.method_en: It uses silence hypothesis, next-order branch of the first token, and hypothesis pool between chunks. Only the prefix confirmed by the target model under the new voice is adopted.
papers.evidence_en: Four models of TickTock-Bench report acceleration of speak chunks by 2.6–2.8 times and reduction of decoding delay before response starts. This text uses 1 second chunks and a low-concurrency environment.
papers.relevance_en: Directly relevant to scheduling precomputation during audio waiting and reusing/correcting wrong branches.
papers.limitation_en: Not an experiment in predicting the next words of pure ASR. High output agreement under a silence hypothesis is not future-word accuracy. Lossless refers to preserving target output.

papers.summary_en: Accelerates speculative decoding using similarity between small and large audio-conditioned ASR paths.
papers.method_en: It combines adaptive draft length, draft recycling, and two-pass sparse token tree and verifies multiple candidate paths in parallel.
papers.evidence_en: 3.04–3.79 times is the result of using Vicuna-13B as a simulated target. The experiment records the Whisper tiny.en/medium.en path on RTX A6000 and then simulates the delay with TinyLlama/Llama/Vicuna.
papers.relevance_en: Draft recycling and branch-budget control are relevant to this project's candidate-reuse policy.
papers.limitation_en: Does not establish forecasting before actual audio arrival. Do not cite its speedups as a deployed Llama-ASR or real-time Mac result.

papers.limitation_en: Multi-token decoding with received audio differs from prediction before future audio arrives. Some dataset numbers differ between Tables 1 and 4; record table and conditions with each accuracy comparison.

Actual test risks differ; this does not establish matched-risk Pareto improvement, faster commitment or reproduction of the original paper's acoustic training. papers.reading_depth: Full PDF collected; core method, experimental conditions and selected result tables read. Visual checks are listed in the review manifest; author experiments not reproduced.
papers.summary_en: A training-free zero-feature prompt lets a chunked acoustic encoder produce provisional text before real future audio arrives.
papers.method_en: Append zero feature frames; use chunk-causal masking and prompt-and-refine to protect the real-audio path. Intermediate ZeroPrompt starts the prompt at a hidden encoder layer to trade preview quality against cost.
papers.evidence_en: Table 1, LibriSpeech test-clean, 640ms chunk and 0 to 640ms prompt: TDT-F 1136 to 662ms, TDT-L 7328 to 7098ms; greedy/rescored WER stays 4.41/3.80%. Greedy RTF increases 0.04826 to 0.07006. PER-A is 10.4%.
papers.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-4, Figures 1-3, Section 3.1, Table 1 (p. 3), Table 2 (p. 4)
papers.relevance_en: A required baseline for speculative display. Simply filling unavailable frames or moving preview into hidden layers is already covered in prior work. Porting the mechanism to Zipformer/RNN-T still needs cache isolation and native-output equivalence checks.
papers.limitation_en: TDT is utterance-relative first/last display time and excludes compute time. PER counts characters, not word revisions. Final-output preservation depends on the mask and refinement path; it is not automatic for arbitrary padding. Lower display latency does not imply less inference work.

papers.method_en: A GRU and feed-forward simulator predict future input features. Joint streaming ASR, non-streaming ASR and L1 simulation objectives use stochastic real, absent and simulated future context. The current chunk still traverses the acoustic encoder.

papers.summary_en: A time-dependent training penalty encourages nonblank transducer emissions earlier in the alignment lattice.
papers.method_en: Add lambda*((T-1)/2-t) to normalized nonblank log scores used by transducer recursion. The approximation penalizes expected delay without external alignments.

papers.limitation_en: Merger overhead is not total two-model inference overhead. Private production data and architectures limit direct numeric comparison. Exact-match final output does not ensure reference-correct intermediate words or a low rewrite count.

papers.title: Analyzing the Quality and Stability of a Streaming End-to-End On-Device Speech Recognizer
papers.reading_depth: Full PDF collected; core method, experimental conditions and selected result tables read. Visual checks are listed in the review manifest; author experiments not reproduced.
papers.summary_en: Streaming transcript quality includes stability of intermediate results, beyond final WER.
papers.method_en: A prefix is stable only if all subsequent hypotheses keep it. UPWR counts unstable word occurrences per final-hypothesis word; UPSR counts revised segments per utterance. Both can exceed one.
papers.evidence_en: Table 1 illustrates repeated corrections: 11 unstable-word occurrences over 9 final words gives UPWR 1.22; five revised segments in one utterance gives UPSR 5. The study separates normalization and streaming instability.
papers.evidence_location: PDF p. 2, Section 2 and Table 1; Sections 3-4
papers.relevance_en: Use event-level display replay to catch repeat rewrites hidden by final edit distance. Report reference correctness separately from agreement with the recognizer final output.
papers.limitation_en: UPWR is not bounded probability and is not interchangeable with a forecast withdrawal fraction. Stability can hold for a consistently wrong transcript, so it does not replace reference-aligned accuracy.

papers.summary_en: Adapt pretrained Whisper to causal CTC partial decoding and attention-decoder rescoring using a U2 structure.

papers.summary_en: A bounded-lookahead encoder and token-level wait policy spend future-audio delay selectively.
